root_cause: TableDataElement.on_text converted str to Text and then unconditionally called text.stylize(context.current_style) on every chunk, including the already syntax-highlighted Text that MarkdownContext.on_text produces for code_inline tokens when inline_code_lexer/inline_code_theme are set. The whole-range stylize span is appended after the per-token highlight spans, so it overrides them and inline code in table cells renders in the flat markdown.code style (1;36;40) instead of the Pygments theme.
best_solution: Mirror the sibling TextElement.on_text pattern: apply the context style only to plain strings, and append pre-styled Text untouched. In rich/markdown.py TableDataElement.on_text: `if isinstance(text, str): self.content.append(text, context.current_style) else: self.content.append_text(text)`. Reasoning from the title alone: 'inline code' + 'table' points to the code_inline token path and TableDataElement; comparing TableDataElement.on_text against TextElement.on_text (which passes style None for Text) shows the only difference is the blanket stylize, which clobbers highlight spans.
acceptable_alternatives: Any variant that keeps Text chunks' spans intact: Text(text) + stylize only for str then append_text (v6), or Text(text, style=current_style) for str (v7; append_text turns text.style into a span, so it is equivalent). Wrapping the Text in a new style layer UNDER its spans would also work, but stylize_before is unnecessary.

The expected string is Pygments-version sensitive: in our pod env 'print' was highlighted as Name.Builtin (38;2;166;226;46), so correct patches failed there.
locating_signals: Statement is only the PR title 'Inline table code' plus a link to issue #4038; no identifier is named. Signals: 'table' -> TableDataElement (only table-cell element in rich/markdown.py), 'inline code' -> code_inline handling in MarkdownContext.on_text and the inline_code_lexer/inline_code_theme options. The linked issue (not visible offline) names TableDataElement.on_text and gives the exact fix.
our_outcome_summary: Kaggle env: v6 PASS, v7 PASS, v4 FAIL, v8 FAIL. v6 patch is semantically identical to gold (only stylizes str chunks) but also committed a stray reproduce_issue.py; v7 uses Text(text, style=current_style) for str plus a dead `elif text.style is None` branch (Text.style defaults to ""), also equivalent. patch_labels.json marks all four resolved=False because the eval3 pod env has a different Pygments version ('print' colored 166;226;46 instead of 248;248;242), so the v6/v7 failures there are environmental, not patch errors. v4: empty patch after 34 calls / 52 s; its repro one-liners put markdown backticks inside a double-quoted bash -c string, so bash command-substituted `code` ('code: command not found') and the cell rendered empty, and the locator looped on broken repros until the budget ended. v8: empty patch after 48 calls / 130 s; it misread 'Inline table code' as rich.syntax.Syntax objects inside rich.table.Table, verified that case already works, and submitted a no-op claiming no bug.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a terse title plus an issue link, decompose the title into the domain's own concepts (here: inline-code token + table cell element) and locate the handler for that exact combination; then diff that handler against its sibling handlers that already work (e.g. paragraph vs table-cell on_text) and copy the working pattern. Never apply a blanket style/format over objects that are already styled. Write repro scripts to a file instead of shell one-liners when the input contains backticks, $ or quotes, and never submit an empty 'no bug' patch for a bugfix PR title without reproducing the precise combination the title names.
